# Chapter 4: The God's Demand

**Applying Guy Sclanders' Methodology**

<details>
<summary><strong>Session Overview</strong></summary>

The fort attack is over -- Vercingetorix, defeated but not destroyed, named the cult
before he was put down (see Session 3's Prologue and the Speak with Dead reveal). The
party now knows what they're looking for: a hidden dungeon somewhere in the forest where
two of Vercingetorix's own chieftains have spent months feeding something they believe
is Mars. This session is that dungeon, start to finish -- a real crawl, not a diplomatic
detour. What the party finds at the bottom is worse than what they expected to find, and
it tells them exactly what Session 5 is going to cost.

**Level:** 5 (crossing the marsh) → 6 (for the rest of the dungeon) → advance to 7 at session end
**Duration:** 4–5 hours
**Key Goal:** Cross the marsh, clear the dungeon, reach the Core Room, and learn what
the cult's ritual actually did
**Theme:** What devotion costs -- the cult didn't get what they wanted. Nobody who
touches this ever does.

<details>
<summary><strong>Guy Sclanders' Principles Applied</strong></summary>

- **Never Present Villain, Now Felt:** the cult chieftains were never really working for
  Brutus or even knowingly for Mars -- they were feeding something wearing his name. The
  party finds out what devotion to that actually looks like once it's "answered."
- **Pressure Cooker:** no clock this session, but every room compounds -- the party
  cannot fully rest between encounters, and the marsh/dungeon design assumes they arrive
  already worn from Session 3's fight.
- **Three Clue Rule:** three separate confirmations that this dungeon is the real target
  -- Vercingetorix's dying words, the sandal buckle/offering evidence from the forest
  (if found), and the supply caches at the marsh entrance.
- **Escalation:** Session 3 was personal (one friend's fall). Session 4 is what an entire
  cult's devotion produces when it succeeds. Session 5 is the god himself.

</details>

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Scene 0: The Marsh</strong></summary>

**Read aloud:**

> *The trees thin out and the ground goes soft underfoot before you see why. Ahead, the
> hillside opens in a mouth -- not a metaphor. A skull carved from the living rock,
> easily twenty feet across, its eye sockets black even at midday. A causeway of bone
> and old skulls runs from between its teeth down into a wide, glowing green marsh that
> splits around the path like water around a stone. The light doesn't flicker like fire.
> It breathes, slow, the way something alive breathes.*

**The crossing:** the bone causeway is the only dry footing across the marsh. Leaving it
means wading through the glowing green water.

::: {.dm-note}
**Marsh hazard, if a character leaves the causeway:** DC 12 Constitution save (active:
each round spent in the glowing water) or gain one level of exhaustion and 1 point of
temporary corruption -- the light isn't fire, it's the same thing that answers to the
name Mars, faintly present in every inch of this place. This should discourage wading
without making it lethal; the causeway itself is always safe.
:::

**Two supply caches** sit at the marsh's near corners, low stone walls around crates and
barrels. DC 11 Wisdom (Investigation) (active: searching a cache) turns up rations gone
green with the same glow, a tally-marked stick counting days (the cult has been here a
long time), and -- in the second cache -- a torn strip of cloth matching the two
chieftains' warband colors, the third and final confirmation this is the right place.

**The encounter:** 3 × **[Banshee](https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/16799-banshee)** (*Monster Manual* p. 23 — CR 4, AC 12, HP 58) rise from the marsh itself as the party crosses — early followers who died tending this place.

::: {.dm-note}
**Combat & Environment:**
- **The Causeway Hazard:** The bone causeway is 5 ft wide. The Banshees float over the water, using *Corrupting Touch* (+4 to hit, 3d6+2 necrotic) and *Horrifying Visage* (DC 13 Wisdom save or frightened). If a PC falls or steps into the glowing water, they trigger the marsh hazard (DC 12 Con save or 1 level of exhaustion + 1 temp corruption).
- **The Wail:** Each Banshee has *Wail* (1/day, DC 13 Constitution save: drops to 0 HP on a failure, or takes 3d6 psychic damage on a success). **Stagger the Wails across rounds**—never trigger more than one Wail in a single round. Telegraph the scream: describe the spirit inhaling the glowing marsh mists, giving players a round to stun, silence, or focus fire.
- **Speed of Play:** With AC 12, the Banshees take heavy damage quickly from a Level 6 party, keeping the combat fast and intense.
:::

</details>


<details>
<summary><strong>Scene 1: The Ossuary</strong></summary>

Past the skull entrance, the dungeon proper begins. The first room, to the west of the
main corridor, is circular and lined with a second skull motif -- smaller, echoing the
entrance.

**Read aloud:**

> *The room ahead is round, and its far wall is shaped like the thing you just walked
> through -- another skull, smaller, teeth picked out in inlaid bone. The floor is a
> carpet of femurs and ribs, stacked with a care that took someone a long time.*

DC 13 Intelligence (History) (active: examining how the bones are arranged): these are
not war dead thrown in a pile. They're sorted -- by size, by age, deliberately. Someone
has been curating this room for months, not years. This matches the tally-stick found at
the marsh.

**The encounter:** 2 × **[Bone Naga](https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/16812-bone-naga)** (*Monster Manual* p. 233 — CR 4, AC 15, HP 58) coiled among the bones, plus 4 × **[Skeleton](https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/17015-skeleton)** (*Monster Manual* p. 272 — CR 1/4, AC 13, HP 13) that animate from the bone floor on initiative count 20.

::: {.dm-note}
**Combat & Tactics:**
- **Skeleton Vulnerability:** Skeletons have official Monster Manual **vulnerability to bludgeoning damage** (MM p. 272). A hit from a mace, warhammer, or sling stone deals double damage, shattering them in a single blow.
- **Bone Naga Spellcasting:** The Nagas rely on spellcasting (DC 12 spell save, +4 spell attack): *hold person*, *ray of sickness* (2d8 poison), and *ray of enfeeblement* to debuff melee fighters.
- **Bite:** +5 to hit, reach 10 ft., 2d6+3 piercing plus 3d6 poison damage.
- **Speed of Play:** With Skeletons dropping in 1 hit to bludgeoning and Nagas having 58 HP, this combat resolves cleanly in 2 rounds.
:::

</details>


<details>
<summary><strong>Scene 2: The Blood-Growth Rooms</strong></summary>

Two connected rooms to the east, walls and floor overtaken by something that isn't mold
and isn't quite flesh -- dense red-black clusters climbing every surface, faintly wet,
faintly warm to the touch.

**Read aloud:**

> *The stone here has stopped being stone. Something has grown over it -- clusters of
> dark red matter, wet-looking, veined, thick as a fist in places and swollen tight.
> They shift, very slightly, when you get close. Not with the room's air currents.*

DC 12 Wisdom (Medicine) or Intelligence (Nature) (active: examining the growths closely):
this is organic, and it's fed -- on blood, deliberately and repeatedly, over a long
period. Whatever grows here was grown on purpose.

**The encounter:** a **[Yochlol](https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/17068-yochlol)** (*Monster Manual* p. 65 — CR 6, AC 15, HP 136) anchored to the pulsating wall-growths, supported by 2 × **[Dretch](https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/16847-dretch)** (*Monster Manual* p. 57 — CR 1/4, AC 11, HP 18).

::: {.dm-note}
**Combat & Tactics:**
- **Yochlol Ambush:** Drops from the ceiling in giant spider form (*Shapechanger*, MM p. 65). Uses *Multiattack* (+6 to hit, 1d6+3 bludgeoning plus 6d6 poison damage) and innate spellcasting (at will *web* DC 14, 1/day *insect plague*). Has Magic Resistance (advantage on saves against spells).
- **Dretches:** Chaff support. They attempt to tie up frontliners using *Fetid Cloud* (1/day, 10-ft radius, DC 11 Constitution save or retching/poisoned). With AC 11 and 18 HP, they drop in 1-2 hits.
:::

</details>


<details>
<summary><strong>Scene 3: The Minor Altar</strong></summary>

The central room of the complex -- a raised dais glowing dull red, four stone pillars
around it at the cardinal points.

**Read aloud:**

> *Four pillars ring a low dais at the room's center, and the dais itself pulses -- not
> light exactly, more like a heartbeat you can see. This isn't the room you came here
> looking for. It feels like a rehearsal for one.*

DC 14 Intelligence (Religion) (active: examining the dais directly): this altar has
never completed a working. It's a practice space -- every mark on it is a false start, a
ritual begun and abandoned. Whatever the cult was building up to happened somewhere
else, not here.

**The encounter:** 3 × **[Shadow Demon](https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/17010-shadow-demon)** (*Monster Manual* p. 64 — CR 4, AC 13, HP 66).

::: {.dm-note}
**Combat & Environment:**
- **Deadly in the Shadows:** In dim light or darkness, Shadow Demons strike with *Claws* (+5 to hit, dealing 4d6+3 psychic damage) and use bonus-action *Shadow Stealth* to hide between the 4 pillars.
- **Official MM Vulnerability & Weakness:** Shadow Demons have official **vulnerability to radiant damage** (MM p. 64) and **Light Sensitivity** (disadvantage on attack rolls and Wisdom (Perception) checks relying on sight in bright light).
- **The Four Stone Braziers:** At the foot of each pillar rests an unlit iron brazier with dry pitch. A character can ignite a brazier as an object interaction / action. Flooding the room with bright light strips their Shadow Stealth and imposes disadvantage on all their attacks!
:::

</details>


<details>
<summary><strong>Scene 4: The Rune Lock</strong></summary>

South of the altar, a room with four tiles set into the floor, each glowing a different
color, arranged in a 2×2 grid.

**Read aloud:**

> *Four tiles are set into the floor here, each etched with a different symbol, each
> lit from beneath in a different color -- cyan, green, magenta, yellow. There's no
> door ahead. Whatever this room is guarding, it's guarding it by making you choose.*

**The puzzle:** the correct sequence is **cyan → green → yellow → magenta**, read as
"beginning, growth, harvest, blood" -- the cult's own private liturgy for what this
dungeon does to whoever spends long enough in it. DC 13 Intelligence (Investigation) or
Wisdom (Insight) (active: examining the tiles' wear patterns): the cyan and green tiles
show more foot traffic than the other two, suggesting an order of use rather than a
single tile being "correct."

**On success:** the tiles dim and a section of wall grinds aside, revealing a short
passage directly to the Gathering Hall.

**On failure (wrong tile pressed):** DC 12 Dexterity save or 2d6 force damage as the
tile briefly inverts, and the sequence resets -- no permanent harm, no lockout, just a
cost in time and HP. This room should never be a hard stop.

::: {.dm-note}
This is the session's breather beat -- no combat by default. If the table is racing
through encounters too easily, an option is to have one Dretch (fled from Scene 2, if it
survived) ambush from hiding while the party is focused on the tiles. Don't force it if
the pacing doesn't need it.
:::

</details>


<details>
<summary><strong>Scene 5: The Gathering Hall</strong></summary>

The largest room in the dungeon -- rows of markers on the floor suggest where a crowd
once knelt, facing a table at the far end still set with rotted offerings.

**Read aloud:**

> *This room was built to hold people. Rows of worn stone mark where dozens once knelt,
> facing a long table at the far end, still laid with offerings gone black with age.
> Whatever congregation gathered here, it hasn't gathered in some time. But something is
> still standing at that table.*

**The reveal:** what's "still standing" are the cult's two chieftains -- or what's left
of them. DC 13 Wisdom (Insight) or Intelligence (Investigation) (active: examining them
before combat starts, if the party hesitates) identifies torn fragments of the same
warband colors found at the marsh cache, confirming their identity.

**The encounter:** 3 × **[Wraith](https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/17064-wraith)** (*Monster Manual* p. 302 — CR 5, AC 13, HP 67) -- the two chieftains and their devoted shield-bearer.

::: {.dm-note}
**Combat & Emotional Beat:**
- **Tragic Opening (Round 1):** The chieftains got what they prayed for, and it consumed them. For the first round, they watch in silence. If addressed, they speak one broken sentence: *"We asked for victory... it took our blood... it starves still..."*
- **Wraith Attacks:** *Life Drain* (+6 to hit, 4d6+3 necrotic, DC 14 Constitution save or HP maximum reduced by damage taken until a long rest). *Incorporeal Movement* allows them to glide through the stone markers to surround the party.
- **Pacing:** To keep combat fast and focused, run this as a straight, brutal clash of blades and necrotic hunger without summoning additional specters.
:::

</details>


<details>
<summary><strong>Scene 6: The Core Room</strong></summary>

Up a curved stair, through an archway ringed by four carved gargoyle faces, into a
circular sanctum. At its center, on a raised dais, a crystal shaped like a jagged star
burns cyan-white.

**Read aloud:**

> *The stair curves up into a perfectly circular chamber. Four stone faces watch from
> the walls at the compass points -- not gods, not ancestors, just teeth and eyes carved
> to be looked at from every angle at once. At the center, on a low dais, a crystal the
> shape of a broken star burns steady and cold. It is the only thing in this entire
> dungeon that looks cared for.*

**What the crystal actually is:** DC 15 Intelligence (Arcana) or Intelligence (Religion)
(active: examining the crystal directly, or automatic once the party has learned what
Vercingetorix revealed): this is the cult's real altar and the marsh's real source. Every
drop of blood spent in every room below was tribute funneled here, into this single
focus -- not to summon Mars, but to keep something that answers to his name fed and
present in the world a little longer. The rooms below aren't separate encounters. They
were all one working, and this was always where it was going.

**The guardian:** 1 × **[Glabrezu](https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/16870-glabrezu)** (*Monster Manual* p. 58 — CR 9, AC 17, HP 157), bound directly to the crystal-star focus.

::: {.dm-note}
**Boss Combat & Tactics:**
- **Innate Spellcasting (DC 16):** Opens with *Darkness* centered on the dais, lunging out at the closest warrior. Uses *Power Word Stun* on the primary damage dealer and *Confusion* if surrounded.
- **Multiattack:** 2 Pincers (+9 to hit, reach 10 ft., 2d10+5 bludgeoning + grapple DC 15) and 2 Fists (+9 to hit, 2d4+5 bludgeoning) or 2 Pincers and casts 1 spell.
- **Speed of Play:** With 6 Level 6 characters focusing fire with magical weapons, smites, and spells, 157 HP is brought down in 2-3 fast, tense rounds!

**The Session's Climax & Rest Transition:**
Once the Glabrezu falls, the room's demonic pressure collapses into a dull, cold humming. The crystal cannot be shattered here -- trying to smash it visibly fails, absorbing whatever strikes it. But the room is now safe.

- **The Long Rest:** The party takes a **Long Rest** in the secured Core Room (consecrated by Tanit or Julia Jana, barricaded by Ursula or Brian).
- **Advancement:** The party **advances to Level 7** during this rest, gaining full HP, all spell slots, and their 4th-level spells, fully prepared for the descent into the abyss in Session 5!
:::

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>OGAS This Session</strong></summary>

**The two chieftains** *(now Wraiths, Scene 5)*
- **Objective (as they once had one):** feed the war-god who could finally give their
  people victories that lasted, not just battles.
- **Goal (this session):** none anymore -- whatever they wanted is gone. What's left
  reacts, not plans.
- **Agenda:** guard the hall they built, unable to leave it or stop.
- **Secret:** they were not lied to about Mars's hunger. They were right about what he
  wanted. They were wrong about what answering it would cost them personally.

**The Glabrezu** *(Core Room Guardian, Scene 6)*
- **Objective:** Maintain the tribute tether and guard the crystal-star focus against any who would disrupt it.
- **Goal (this session):** Crush intruders in the dais darkness; protect the four gargoyle conduits.
- **Agenda:** Fights to the death; will not pursue retreating players beyond the antechamber archway.
- **Secret:** It is not summoned from the Abyss by mortals -- it was pulled through the veil by the sheer density of blood offered here, a living manifestation of Mars's escalating hunger.

</details>
